Here is the issue description:
# [otbn,dv] Collecting coverage fails for various tests
### Description
The current [OTBN Simulation Results page](https://nightly.reports.lowrisc.org/opentitan_weekly_earlgrey/2025_11_02/hw/ip/otbn/dv/uvm/report.html) reports many OTBN tests as failing for the master branch. For example the otbn_smoke or otbn_single test.
When I run these tests locally with DV sim but without coverage reporting, they pass (I tested otbn_smoke, otbn_single and otbn_multi_err). I run the tests with:
```
util/dvsim/dvsim.py hw/ip/otbn/dv/uvm/otbn_sim_cfg.hjson -i otbn_smoke
```
These tests fail when coverage is enabled (with the `--cov` argument) because illegal values are sampled for the mnemonic coverpoints of the instruction covergroups. An example for such a coverpoint is:
https://github.com/lowRISC/opentitan/blob/9baed2bba4eccd325684c27b74049391d865c76f/hw/ip/otbn/dv/uvm/env/otbn_env_cov.sv#L1185-L1200
I pinpointed the error down to the commit e9986ef486. This commit changes the macro `DEF_MNEM_BIN` such that quotes are added around the mnemonic to satisfy Verissimo. As a consequence, the bin is looking for mnemonic values like `"addi"` (with the quotes). However, the sample function of the covergroup is always called with the mnemonic without quotes, e.g., the passed value is `addi` (without quotes). The passed value is then handled as an illegal value and thus an error is reported.
When I revert the commit, the tests pass again.
@rswarbrick Can you please explain to me why the quotes are required? And if they are, how the setup can be adapted such that mnemonics with quotes are passed/generated?

2290   // Handle coverage for external (bus-accessible) CSRs.
2291   //
2292   // This runs just before calling predict to update the RAL model, so the old value of the CSR can
2293   // be read with csr.get_mirrored_value().
2294   function void on_ext_csr_access(uvm_reg csr, otbn_env_pkg::access_e access_type,
2295                                   logic [31:0] data, operational_state_e state);
2296 
2297     csr_str_t csr_name        = csr_str_t'(csr.get_name());
2298     bit track_write_then_read = 1'b0;
2299 
2300     case (csr_name)
2301       "cmd": begin
2302         ext_csr_cmd_cg.sample(otbn_pkg::cmd_e'(data), access_type, state);
2303       end
2304       "ctrl": begin
2305         track_write_then_read = 1'b1;
2306         ext_csr_ctrl_cg.sample(data[0], access_type, state);
2307       end
2308       "status": begin
2309         ext_csr_status_cg.sample(otbn_pkg::status_e'(data), access_type);
2310       end
2311       "err_bits": begin
2312         last_err_bits = data;
2313         ext_csr_err_bits_cg.sample(otbn_pkg::err_bits_t'(data),
2314                                    csr.get_mirrored_value(), access_type, state);
2315       end
2316       "fatal_alert_cause": begin
2317         ext_csr_fatal_alert_cause_cg.sample(data, access_type, state);
2318 
2319         // If we read a FATAL_ALERT_CAUSE of (1 << 7) = FATAL_SOFTWARE and we're in a locked state
2320         // then we should sample promoted_err_cg to track what SW error was promoted.
2321         if ((state == OperationalStateLocked) &&
2322             (access_type == AccessSoftwareRead) &&
2323             (data == (1 << 7))) begin
2324           promoted_err_cg.sample(last_err_bits[5:0]);
2325         end
2326       end
2327       "insn_cnt": begin
2328         ext_csr_insn_cnt_cg.sample(data, csr.get_mirrored_value(), access_type, state);
2329       end
2330       "load_checksum": begin
2331         track_write_then_read = 1'b1;
2332 
2333         // Special handling for the "write; update; read" sequence.
2334         case (wur_state)
2335           WUR_IDLE: begin
2336             // The WUR_IDLE -> WUR_WRITTEN_CSR transition should happen if we see a write to the
2337             // register that will change its value and we're in an operational state where it will
2338             // take effect.
2339             if ((data != csr.get_mirrored_value()) &&
2340                 (access_type == AccessSoftwareWrite) &&
2341                 (state == OperationalStateIdle)) begin
2342               wur_state = WUR_WRITTEN_CSR;
2343             end
2344           end
2345           WUR_WRITTEN_CSR: begin
2346             // We can't leave the WUR_WRITTEN_CSR state by accessing the CSR (see on_mem_write())
2347           end
2348           WUR_UPDATED_MEM: begin
2349             // If we read the CSR after updating memory, sample from the covergroup and go back to
2350             // WUR_IDLE.
2351             if (access_type == AccessSoftwareRead) begin
2352               ext_csr_load_checksum_wur_cg.sample();
2353               wur_state = WUR_IDLE;
2354             end
2355           end
2356           default: `DV_CHECK_FATAL(0)
2357         endcase
2358       end
2359       default: ; // We only track some registers with functional coverage.
2360     endcase
2361 
2362     // Track "write then read" across operational states
2363     if (track_write_then_read) begin
2364       if (access_type == AccessSoftwareWrite) begin
2365         on_write_to_wr_csr(csr, data, state);
2366       end else begin
2367         if (last_write_state.exists(csr_name)) begin
2368           ext_csr_wr_operational_state_cg.sample(csr_name, last_write_state[csr_name]);
2369         end
2370       end
2371     end
2372   endfunction

2394   // Handle coverage for an instruction that was executed
2395   //
2396   // Almost all the tracking is done based on rtl_item, which comes from the DUT. Our only use for
2397   // iss_item is to extract the instruction mnemonic (to avoid needing it, we'd have to implement a
2398   // decoder in the coverage code, which doesn't seem like the right thing to do).
2399   //
2400   function void on_insn(otbn_model_item iss_item, otbn_trace_item rtl_item);
2401     string encoding;
2402 
2403     mnem_str_t   mnem;
2404     logic [31:0] insn_data;
2405     logic [31:0] loop_bodysize;
2406     logic        call_stack_push, call_stack_pop, call_stack_overflow, call_stack_underflow;
2407 
2408     logic signed [31:0] addr;
2409     logic [9:0]         imm10;
2410     logic [11:0]        imm12;
2411     logic [12:0]        imm13;
2412     logic [14:0]        imm15;
2413     logic [20:0]        imm21;
2414 
2415     // Since iss_item and rtl_item have come in separately, we do a quick check here to make sure
2416     // they actually match the same instruction.
2417     `DV_CHECK_EQ(iss_item.insn_addr, rtl_item.insn_addr)
2418 
2419     // iss_item.mnemonic is a "string". We have to cast this to an integral type (mnem_str_t) to use
2420     // it for bins in a coverpoint. This type is chosen to be long enough to hold each valid
2421     // mnemonic, but it can't hurt to make absolutely sure that nothing overflows.
2422     `DV_CHECK_FATAL(iss_item.mnemonic.len() <= MNEM_STR_LEN)
2423 
2424     mnem = mnem_str_t'(iss_item.mnemonic);
2425     insn_data = rtl_item.insn_data;
2426 
2427     // Track and catch when we are on the top of the instruction memory and have a straight-line
2428     // instruction.
2429     insn_addr_cg.sample(mnem, rtl_item.insn_addr);
2430 
2431     // Call stack tracking. Some instructions want to know whether they are over- or under-flowing
2432     // the call stack so, as well as sampling in the call_stack_cg covergroup, we also compute those
2433     // flags which we'll use below.
2434     call_stack_cg.sample(rtl_item.call_stack_flags, rtl_item.call_stack_fullness);
2435 
2436     call_stack_push = rtl_item.call_stack_flags.push;
2437     call_stack_pop = rtl_item.call_stack_flags.pop_a | rtl_item.call_stack_flags.pop_b;
2438 
2439     call_stack_overflow = ((rtl_item.call_stack_fullness == StackFull) &&
2440                            call_stack_push && !call_stack_pop);
2441     call_stack_underflow = (rtl_item.call_stack_fullness == StackEmpty) && call_stack_pop;
2442 
2443     // Flag set/clear tracking
2444     for (int fg = 0; fg < 2; fg++) begin
2445       if (rtl_item.flags_write_valid[fg]) begin
2446         flag_write_cg.sample(fg[0], rtl_item.flags_read_data[fg], rtl_item.flags_write_data[fg]);
2447       end
2448     end
2449 
2450     // Track pairwise instructions. last_mnem is zero if this is the first instruction since
2451     // starting an operation.
2452     if (last_mnem != '0) begin
2453       pairwise_insn_cg.sample(last_mnem, mnem);
2454     end
2455     last_mnem = mnem;
2456 
2457     // Per-encoding coverage. First, use insn_encodings to find the encoding for the instruction.
2458     // Every instruction mnemonic should have an associated encoding schema.
2459     encoding = insn_encodings[mnem];
2460     case (encoding)
2461       "bna":
2462         enc_bna_cg.sample(mnem, insn_data,
2463                           rtl_item.wdr_operand_a, rtl_item.wdr_operand_b,
2464                           rtl_item.flags_write_data, rtl_item.wdr_write_data);
2465       "bnaf":
2466         enc_bnaf_cg.sample(mnem, insn_data,
2467                            rtl_item.wdr_operand_a, rtl_item.wdr_operand_b,
2468                            rtl_item.flags_write_data);
2469       "bnai":
2470         enc_bnai_cg.sample(mnem, insn_data,
2471                            rtl_item.wdr_operand_a,
2472                            rtl_item.flags_write_data);
2473       "bnam":
2474         enc_bnam_cg.sample(mnem, insn_data, rtl_item.wdr_operand_a, rtl_item.wdr_operand_b);
2475       "bnan":
2476         enc_bnan_cg.sample(mnem, insn_data,
2477                            rtl_item.wdr_operand_a,
2478                            rtl_item.flags_write_data,
2479                            rtl_item.wdr_write_data);
2480       "bnaq":
2481         enc_bnaq_cg.sample(mnem, insn_data, rtl_item.wdr_operand_a, rtl_item.wdr_operand_b);
2482       "bnaqs":
2483         enc_bnaqs_cg.sample(mnem, insn_data,
2484                             rtl_item.wdr_operand_a, rtl_item.wdr_operand_b,
2485                             rtl_item.flags_write_data);
2486       "bnaqw":
2487         enc_bnaqw_cg.sample(mnem, insn_data,
2488                             rtl_item.wdr_operand_a, rtl_item.wdr_operand_b,
2489                             rtl_item.flags_write_data);
2490       "bnc":
2491         enc_bnc_cg.sample(mnem, insn_data,
2492                           rtl_item.wdr_operand_a, rtl_item.wdr_operand_b,
2493                           rtl_item.flags_write_data);
2494       "bnmov":
2495         enc_bnmov_cg.sample(mnem, insn_data, rtl_item.wdr_operand_a);
2496       "bnmovr":
2497         enc_bnmovr_cg.sample(mnem, insn_data, rtl_item.gpr_operand_a, rtl_item.gpr_operand_b);
2498       "bnr":
2499         enc_bnr_cg.sample(mnem, insn_data, rtl_item.wdr_operand_a, rtl_item.wdr_operand_b);
2500       "bns":
2501         enc_bns_cg.sample(mnem, insn_data,
2502                           rtl_item.wdr_operand_a, rtl_item.wdr_operand_b,
2503                           rtl_item.flags_read_data);
2504       "bnxid":
2505         enc_bnxid_cg.sample(mnem, insn_data, rtl_item.gpr_operand_a, rtl_item.gpr_operand_b);
2506       "B":
2507         enc_b_cg.sample(mnem, insn_data, rtl_item.gpr_operand_a, rtl_item.gpr_operand_b);
2508       "ecall":
2509         enc_ecall_cg.sample(mnem, insn_data);
2510       "I":
2511         enc_i_cg.sample(mnem, insn_data, rtl_item.gpr_operand_a);
2512       "Is":
2513         enc_is_cg.sample(mnem, insn_data, rtl_item.gpr_operand_a);
2514       "J":
2515         enc_j_cg.sample(mnem, insn_data);
2516       "loop":
2517         enc_loop_cg.sample(mnem, insn_data, rtl_item.gpr_operand_a);
2518       "loopi":
2519         enc_loopi_cg.sample(mnem, insn_data);
2520       "R":
2521         enc_r_cg.sample(mnem, insn_data, rtl_item.gpr_operand_a, rtl_item.gpr_operand_b);
2522       "S":
2523         enc_s_cg.sample(mnem, insn_data, rtl_item.gpr_operand_a, rtl_item.gpr_operand_b);
2524       "U":
2525         enc_u_cg.sample(mnem, insn_data);
2526       "wcsr":
2527         enc_wcsr_cg.sample(mnem, insn_data);
2528       "dummy":
2529         // Bad instruction: no encoding-level coverage.
2530         ;
2531       default: `dv_fatal($sformatf("Unknown encoding (%0s) for instruction `%0s'", encoding, mnem),
2532                          `gfn)
2533     endcase
2534 
2535     // LOOP and LOOPI instructions store bodysize as an immediate in bits 31:20, but shifted by 1
2536     // (so a bodysize of 1 is encoded as 0 etc.)
2537     loop_bodysize = 32'(insn_data[31:20]) + 32'd1;
2538 
2539     // Instruction-specific coverage.
2540     case (mnem)
2541       mnem_add, mnem_sub:
2542         insn_addsub_cg.sample(mnem, rtl_item.gpr_operand_a, rtl_item.gpr_operand_b);
2543       mnem_addi:
2544         insn_addi_cg.sample(insn_data, rtl_item.gpr_operand_a);
2545       mnem_sll:
2546         insn_sll_cg.sample(rtl_item.gpr_operand_a, rtl_item.gpr_operand_b);
2547       mnem_slli:
2548         insn_slli_cg.sample(insn_data, rtl_item.gpr_operand_a);
2549       mnem_srl:
2550         insn_srl_cg.sample(rtl_item.gpr_operand_a, rtl_item.gpr_operand_b);
2551       mnem_srli:
2552         insn_srli_cg.sample(insn_data, rtl_item.gpr_operand_a);
2553       mnem_sra:
2554         insn_sra_cg.sample(rtl_item.gpr_operand_a, rtl_item.gpr_operand_b);
2555       mnem_srai:
2556         insn_srai_cg.sample(insn_data, rtl_item.gpr_operand_a);
2557       mnem_and, mnem_andi, mnem_or, mnem_ori, mnem_xor, mnem_xori:
2558         // This covergroup tracks write data, so we only sample when GRD is nonzero
2559         if (insn_data[11:7] != 0) begin
2560           insn_log_binop_cg.sample(mnem, insn_data, rtl_item.gpr_write_data);
2561         end
2562       mnem_lw: begin
2563         imm12 = insn_data[31:20];
2564         addr = $signed(rtl_item.gpr_operand_a) + $signed(imm12);
2565         insn_xw_cg.sample(mnem,
2566                           imm12,
2567                           insn_data[19:15] /* grs1 */,
2568                           insn_data[11:7] /* grd */,
2569                           rtl_item.gpr_operand_a,
2570                           addr,
2571                           rtl_item.call_stack_fullness,
2572                           call_stack_underflow);
2573       end
2574       mnem_sw: begin
2575         imm12 = {insn_data[31:25], insn_data[11:7]};
2576         addr = $signed(rtl_item.gpr_operand_a) + $signed(imm12);
2577         insn_xw_cg.sample(mnem,
2578                           imm12,
2579                           insn_data[19:15] /* grs1 */,
2580                           insn_data[24:20] /* grs2 */,
2581                           rtl_item.gpr_operand_a,
2582                           addr,
2583                           rtl_item.call_stack_fullness,
2584                           call_stack_underflow);
2585       end
2586       mnem_beq, mnem_bne: begin
2587         imm13 = {insn_data[31], insn_data[7], insn_data[30:25], insn_data[11:8], 1'b0};
2588         addr = $signed(rtl_item.insn_addr) + $signed(imm13);
2589         insn_bxx_cg.sample(mnem,
2590                            rtl_item.insn_addr,
2591                            imm13,
2592                            rtl_item.gpr_operand_a,
2593                            rtl_item.gpr_operand_b,
2594                            addr,
2595                            rtl_item.at_current_loop_end_insn,
2596                            call_stack_underflow);
2597       end
2598       mnem_jal: begin
2599         imm21 = {insn_data[31], insn_data[19:12], insn_data[20], insn_data[30:21], 1'b0};
2600         addr = $signed(rtl_item.insn_addr) + $signed(imm21);
2601         insn_jal_cg.sample(rtl_item.insn_addr,
2602                            imm21,
2603                            addr,
2604                            rtl_item.at_current_loop_end_insn,
2605                            call_stack_overflow);
2606       end
2607       mnem_jalr: begin
2608         imm12 = insn_data[31:20];
2609         addr = $signed(rtl_item.gpr_operand_a) + $signed(imm12);
2610         insn_jalr_cg.sample(rtl_item.insn_addr,
2611                             imm12,
2612                             addr,
2613                             rtl_item.gpr_operand_a,
2614                             rtl_item.at_current_loop_end_insn,
2615                             call_stack_underflow,
2616                             call_stack_overflow);
2617       end
2618       mnem_csrrs:
2619         insn_csrrs_cg.sample(insn_data,
2620                              rtl_item.gpr_operand_a,
2621                              rtl_item.call_stack_fullness);
2622       mnem_csrrw:
2623         insn_csrrw_cg.sample(insn_data,
2624                              rtl_item.call_stack_fullness);
2625       mnem_loop:
2626         insn_loop_cg.sample(rtl_item.insn_addr,
2627                             insn_data,
2628                             rtl_item.gpr_operand_a,
2629                             rtl_item.loop_stack_fullness,
2630                             rtl_item.current_loop_end,
2631                             loop_bodysize,
2632                             rtl_item.at_current_loop_end_insn,
2633                             call_stack_underflow);
2634       mnem_loopi: begin
2635         imm10 = {insn_data[19:15], insn_data[11:7]};
2636         insn_loopi_cg.sample(rtl_item.insn_addr,
2637                              insn_data,
2638                              rtl_item.loop_stack_fullness,
2639                              rtl_item.current_loop_end,
2640                              imm10,
2641                              loop_bodysize,
2642                              rtl_item.at_current_loop_end_insn);
2643       end
2644       mnem_bn_addc:
2645         insn_bn_addc_cg.sample(insn_data,
2646                                rtl_item.flags_read_data);
2647       mnem_bn_addm:
2648         insn_bn_addm_cg.sample(insn_data,
2649                                rtl_item.wdr_operand_a,
2650                                rtl_item.wdr_operand_b,
2651                                rtl_item.mod);
2652       mnem_bn_mulqacc, mnem_bn_mulqacc_so, mnem_bn_mulqacc_wo:
2653         insn_bn_mulqaccx_cg.sample(mnem,
2654                                    rtl_item.new_acc_extended);
2655       mnem_bn_subb, mnem_bn_cmpb:
2656         insn_bn_subcmpb_cg.sample(mnem,
2657                                   insn_data,
2658                                   rtl_item.flags_read_data);
2659       mnem_bn_subm:
2660         insn_bn_subm_cg.sample(insn_data,
2661                                rtl_item.wdr_operand_a,
2662                                rtl_item.wdr_operand_b,
2663                                rtl_item.mod);
2664       mnem_bn_lid, mnem_bn_sid: begin
2665         logic       inc_both = insn_data[8] && insn_data[7];
2666         logic [4:0] grs1 = insn_data[19:15];
2667         logic [4:0] grx2 = insn_data[24:20]; // Either GRD or GRS2
2668         logic       local_x1_uflow;
2669 
2670         imm15 = {insn_data[11:9], insn_data[31:25], 5'b0};
2671         addr = $signed(rtl_item.gpr_operand_a) + $signed(imm15);
2672 
2673         // Compute our own definition of call_stack_underflow. This should match the existing one if
2674         // !inc_both. However, when both increments are set the RTL decoder squashes the call stack
2675         // update flags so we have to figure them out ourselves.
2676         local_x1_uflow = (rtl_item.call_stack_fullness == StackEmpty) &&
2677                          ((grs1 == 5'd1) || (grx2 == 5'd1));
2678         `DV_CHECK_FATAL(local_x1_uflow || !call_stack_underflow)
2679         `DV_CHECK_FATAL(inc_both || call_stack_underflow || !local_x1_uflow)
2680 
2681         insn_bn_xid_cg.sample(mnem,
2682                               imm15,
2683                               rtl_item.gpr_operand_a,
2684                               rtl_item.gpr_operand_b,
2685                               addr,
2686                               inc_both,
2687                               grs1,
2688                               grx2,
2689                               local_x1_uflow);
2690       end
2691       mnem_bn_movr: begin
2692         logic       inc_both = insn_data[9] && insn_data[7];
2693         logic [4:0] grs = insn_data[19:15];
2694         logic [4:0] grd = insn_data[24:20];
2695         logic       local_x1_uflow;
2696 
2697         // Compute our own definition of call_stack_underflow. This should match the existing one if
2698         // !inc_both. However, when both increments are set the RTL decoder squashes the call stack
2699         // update flags so we have to figure them out ourselves.
2700         local_x1_uflow = (rtl_item.call_stack_fullness == StackEmpty) &&
2701                          ((grs == 5'd1) || (grd == 5'd1));
2702         `DV_CHECK_FATAL(local_x1_uflow || !call_stack_underflow)
